repairs.value: Licona argues that grief cannot explain James or Paul, Paul’s alleged guilt lacks evidence, and Carrier’s unsupported appearance calculus therefore fails to naturalize the reported appearances.

Strongest feature: Licona tests Carrier’s mechanisms against adverse witnesses, contrasting grief with James and Paul and challenging Paul’s hypothesized guilt through his persecutor résumé. Principal limitation: His attack on the distribution premise overstates its unsupportedness, because Carrier had already grounded selectivity in the expectation that a saving deity would appear broadly and later sharpened that rationale through divine compassion, so rhetorical questions do not defeat the comparison. Live burden: Evaluators must determine whether Licona’s counterevidence lowers guilt-based hallucination, and whether Carrier’s theological expectation supplies defensible comparative probability rather than personal intuition. Locked score: The fixed score of 85 rewards pressure on James, Paul, and speculative psychological triggers, while withholding higher credit because Carrier’s distribution rationale receives insufficient engagement.
